title: The handover manifest
summary: The asset list becomes the document you actually receive: a paper handover manifest hung from the Index Spine on the graphite chapter (its left edge is the spine, as in the nav's sheet), where six assets sit in a catalogue ledger, each custody box fills as the asset changes hands from Kelwin to you, one row opens onto its contents, and the sheet closes on its terms and a sign-off carrying the real lockup — ownership shown as an artifact rather than claimed in a table, where today's version is a described list with a terms card.

reference.borrowed: Waka Waka's catalogue-index cadence: evenly spaced rows with a tiny catalogue number flush left, the object name in medium weight, the material in a second column and a right-aligned parenthetical. There is no column header, no description and no card, so the authority comes from rhythm and numbering alone.
reference.kelwin: Waka Waka's catalogue cadence (tiny number · object · material · a quiet right-hand mark) stays as the row rhythm, set on the page's own cols 4–12 inside B's one inset plate for this stretch of the page: a flat paper sheet (data-surface light) hung from the Index Spine on the graphite section. Its left edge IS the spine and its top-left corner carries the joint square, the grammar of the nav's mega sheet; it runs out to the page edge. The sheet is the handover manifest the body copy promises: a mono masthead ('HANDOVER MANIFEST · SPECIMEN' / 'Issued at handover · 06 assets · 01 owner') over an ink rule, mono column heads (Asset · Format · Custody), six rows (N·01–06, 24px normal-width asset, 17px format, a custody box + 'YOURS', a hairline +), one row open onto its descriptor and a four-line specimen contents list, then an ink rule into the terms (Ownership · Deprecation risk · Handover) and a sign-off: 'Handed over by' the real .km-logo lockup, 'Received by' your team on a signature line. Head per the founder spec inside B's grammar (10 + red-square 'Ownership', 88px 'When we leave, / the system stays.' with the light muted clause, 48×2 red rule) with the source coda and a quiet door to the method. Red appears only in the label square and the rule.

motion: entrance: the opening rule draws spine → right margin (900ms), the joint and index fade in, the statement rises 12px with its light clause 160ms behind, the red rule draws, body and side note fade.

the sheet hangs open from the spine left → right (clip-path, 1000ms --ease-out, from 0.82s) like every opening rule; its masthead and column heads fade in, each row's hairline draws from the spine (600ms, 60ms stagger) as its index, asset, format and toggle fade in; the terms rule draws and the terms and 'Handed over by' lockup fade in.

the one orchestrated moment (custody changes hands): from 2.05s, row by row top-down at 150ms, each custody box fills from an open grey square to solid ink while its holder crossfades 'KELWIN' → 'YOURS' (360ms --ease-inout); then the 'Received by' signature line draws (700ms) and 'Your team' appears on it.
ledger open: at about 3.35s N·01 opens in place (height + opacity 360ms --ease-inout, '+' turning to '−') onto its descriptor and specimen contents.

interaction: every row opens in place on click, one at a time, each onto its own contents. A hovered row fills --panel from the spine to the margin and its asset shifts 8px right; the quiet door's underline draws from the left and its arrow moves 3px.
on the live site: the spine index is sticky and crossfades as sections pass; the handover plays once when the sheet is 50% visible. Reduced motion shows the final state: every box filled, N·01 open.
notes: Critics held the previous custody-line ledger at proprietary 7 because its skeleton still read as a table. Rebuilt as an object: the ledger now lives on B's inset plate (used once in this stretch — the CTA's red inset is three sections later) as a specimen of the actual handover manifest, so the section shows the thing you keep rather than listing it. The sheet's left edge is the Index Spine and it runs to the page edge, exactly as the nav's paper sheet does, so it reads as B's own device. Contents lists are illustrative headings drawn from each asset's source description, labelled SPECIMEN; asset names, formats, descriptors, coda and terms come from AssetInventory.tsx. 'Received by · Your team' is a sign-off field, not a claim. The quiet door now goes to the method ('How the handover works →') instead of /audit, per the two-door rule. Shared B head: 64px light index + red-square caps label (Mona 500, 11px, .18em), 88px statement at weight 430 / −0.018em with one light (300) muted clause, the 48×2 red rule, 18/30 lede, 128px top and bottom padding (the live site keeps B's 200px). Mockup slice: the 1400px stage crops most of the bottom padding.
